subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Team,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn about FinPay's real-time risk scoring use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Peak traffic: ~400 requests/sec sustained during peak windows, up to ~1,000 req/sec for short bursts (1-5m)
- Typical steady-state: ~100 qps
- Latency targets: p50 < 30ms, p95 <= 100ms (hard requirement for checkout flows)
- Data: transaction-level events, PII is redacted in-app but you will need audit logs retained for 12 months

Key recommendation (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest to prototype and goes into production quickly with autoscaling; good for PoC and early rollout.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need guaranteed throughput and tighter p95 latency SLOs (reserved GPU pool, predictable cold-start behavior, lower jitter). Matches your sustained + burst profile if you commit to a reserved pool.
- Private VPC/on-prem: only necessary if your security/compliance team requires fully private networking or on-prem data residency.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a preliminary capacity_estimate.xlsx and a sample SLA_draft_FinPay_v1.pdf for your procurement review.
2) Proposed: run a 48-hour hosted performance validation at your typical traffic pattern to collect real p50/p95 numbers. If hosted meets your p95 target across bursts we can remain on hosted; otherwise move to Dedicated (we can do a canary migration).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (Solutions Eng) & Dylan (Infra) to align on test profile and model variant (will take ~45-60m).

Would Thursday or Friday this week work for the deep-dive? I can also loop in our procurement specialist if you want to review the SLA now.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick recap — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/engineering: 

- Does the hosted API support prefix/KV caching and autoscaling behavior that would help during price-check spikes?
- Ballpark: what is the expected monthly delta between hosted and a Dedicated reserved pool that covers ~1,000 peak? A rough range is fine.
- Timeline constraints: our procurement window wants a target go-live by late July if we decide to commit to Dedicated. How long is lead time for reserved capacity?

Procurement attached our internal timeline (procurement_schedule.pdf) — happy to review the SLA draft and the capacity estimate with your team.

If it helps, we're open to starting on hosted for the PoC and moving to Dedicated after validation, assuming migration path is straightforward.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — recap & next steps

Alex — great questions. Short answers up front, details below:
- Hosted does support autoscaling and prefix/KV caching; however, guaranteed p95 during sustained bursts is not SLA-backed on hosted.
- Ballpark monthly delta (very rough): hosted (scale-based billing) for your expected volume ~$40k–$70k/month depending on token usage and caching; Dedicated reserved capacity to cover sustained 400 qps with burst headroom to 1,000 qps is roughly $80k–$140k/month (committed), with lower per-token cost and more predictable latency. We'll refine after we size the exact GPU pool.
- Dedicated lead time: typically 4–6 weeks from commitment to provisioning (depends on region and capacity).

More detail:
- Performance tradeoffs: Hosted autoscaling is fast and works well for many customers, but multi-tenant jitter and cold-starts during large bursts can increase p95. Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool, predictable KV cache residency, and we can tune kernel selection/quantization for your model variant to reduce jitter.
- Hybrid approach (recommended): start with hosted for a 48-hour PoC to validate p95/p50 under your workload and then, if needed, schedule Dedicated provisioning. Migration path is tested by our infra team (canary rollout, prefix cache warm-up) and typically smooth.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Book 45–60m deep-dive this week so Marissa/Dylan can confirm test profile and quick configuration options (suggest Thu 27 May 2pm PT or Fri 28 May 11am PT).
2) We run a 48-hour hosted perf run using your traffic replay (we can host the test runner or you can push traffic).
3) If p95 > 100ms under peak bursts, we move to Dedicated and I'll get you an updated committed-capacity quote and timeline.

I'll work on tightening the capacity_estimate.xlsx ranges and prepare a short migration checklist. If you're good with the plan, I'll schedule the deep-dive and ask Marissa to prepare an initial load-test script.

Thanks,
Neha

Neha
